newsitem.title: UK: National Grid shares up on cost-cutting plans.
newsitem.headline: National Grid shares up on cost-cutting plans.

text.p: British electricity transmission network National Grid Group Plc on Tuesday reported a drop in first-half pre-tax profits but its shares rose as it outlined plans to cut costs.
National Grid's pre-tax profit dropped to 292.7 million pounds ($492.7 million) in the six months to September 30, from 335.5 million pounds in the same period a year ago.
The figures were in line with analysts' forecasts which ranged from 279 to 304 million pounds.

Shares in the company were 6-1/2p higher at 205-1/2p in a firm London market as investors welcomed news of a streamlining programme to cut National Grid's cost base by an average of about six percent per year in real terms.
The company also said it expected to deliver real growth in dividend per share close to the level implied for the periods ended March 1996 and 1997.
National Grid added that it expected to pay a final dividend of 6.68 pence per share, making a total dividend of 11.13 pence per share for the year.

The company said the strength of the forward order book for its Energis telecommunications service supported the view that Energis would be profitable before interest, tax and depreciation for the year ending March 1998. ($1=.5941 Pound)
